about.title: Sources & methodology
about.intro: Clack logs the trains you ride. Timetables, actual times and maps come from open data.

sources.trafikverket: Trafikverket Open API: actual times, delays, platforms, stations and live positions.
sources.gtfsSverige2: Trafiklab GTFS Sverige 2 (CC0): historical timetables back to 2012.
sources.entur: Entur (Norway), under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD): rail timetables, stations, live positions, delays, actual times and departure boards.
sources.osm: Rail network and map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Basemap tiles by Protomaps.
sources.stationMaps: Station maps: drafted from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors) and edited by hand; the map data is offered under the ODbL like OpenStreetMap itself. Walking times are worked out from the map, not timed on site. Opening hours are as listed and may differ on holidays.
sources.onboard: On board: catering and same-day notices come from Trafikverket for each departure; everything marked "Typically" comes from the operator's own pages, with the date it was checked.

about.delaysBody: Green: on time or early. Yellow: 1–15 min late. Amber: 16–30 min. Red: more than 30 min. A train counts as on time in your stats when it arrives at most {{max}} minutes late.
about.co2Body: Distance along the track × (comparison factor − train factor). Factors are well-to-wheel g CO₂e per passenger-km from IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute, report U11173 (2026). Norwegian trips use the same factors for now: we haven’t yet checked a Norwegian source.
